blocks.orig: Imagine thousands of wildebeests and zebras together in a herd, all moaning and braying in their distinctive sounds, kicking up dust and protecting each other from the surrounding predators. Impressive as this may be (and trust us – it is!), if you add a river to that equation, it becomes truly a unique spectacle! This is the yearly Mara River crossing of the Great Wildebeest Migration in northern Serengeti, which only occurs from late July to early October.
blocks.html: Picture a herd of thousands of wildebeests and zebras, groaning and braying with their unmistakable calls, throwing up dust and shielding one another from the predators all around. That alone is impressive (believe us, it really is!), but put a river in their path and it turns into a truly one-of-a-kind spectacle! This is the annual Mara River crossing of the Great Wildebeest Migration in the northern Serengeti, which happens only between late July and early October.

blocks.orig: This route takes you straight to the area of this apotheosis of nature, where – if you’re fortunate – you might see the herds risking their lives in a river full of crocs. Crocs? Indeed, those nasty buggers, and no, this is not a route for the faint-hearted! Oh, and did we mention it also passes by the elephant-packed Tarangire and the impressive Ngorongoro crater on the way back?
blocks.html: On this route you travel directly to the scene of this natural climax, where, with some luck, you may watch the herds risk their lives in a river teeming with crocs. Crocs? Yes, those nasty creatures, so this is certainly no route for the faint-hearted! And did we say that on the return leg you also pass the elephant-filled Tarangire and the impressive Ngorongoro crater?

blocks.orig: Many travelers ask us when the best time is to visit Tanzania. The answer is … there is not one right answer. It depends on what you want to see, where you want to go, your budget and interests. Please find a comprehensive guide on when is the best time to visit Tanzania here.
blocks.html: A question we hear from many travellers is when to go to Tanzania. The truth is that no single answer fits everyone: it comes down to what you hope to see, where you would like to travel, your budget and your interests. You will find a detailed guide on the best time to visit Tanzania here.

blocks.orig: Our safaris in Tanzania offer an opportunity to explore the country’s incredible wildlife and stunning landscapes. We specialize in private safaris, which means you have a 4×4 Landcruiser or jeep all to yourselves. You have the flexibility to decide when the safari starts and ends, and our experienced guides can help you make that decision on the day of your adventure. Whether you want to witness the animals at their most active during sunrise and sunset when temperatures are pleasant, or if you fancy ending the day by the pool, it’s entirely up to you. Tanzania’s diverse wildlife is active at various times of the day, so you’ll have plenty of opportunities to spot the animals in action.
blocks.html: With our safaris you get the chance to discover Tanzania’s remarkable wildlife and beautiful scenery. Private safaris are our speciality, so the 4×4 Landcruiser or jeep is yours alone. You choose when each day’s safari begins and finishes, and our experienced guides are happy to help you decide on the day itself. Perhaps you want to see the animals when they are most active around sunrise and sunset, while the temperatures are mild, or perhaps you would rather finish the afternoon at the pool: the choice is yours. Because Tanzania’s varied wildlife is active at different times of day, you’ll have many chances to watch animals on the move.

blocks.orig: Absolutely, Tanzania is renowned as one of the prime destinations to encounter the Big Five. These magnificent creatures—lion, leopard, elephant, rhinoceros, and buffalo—can be observed in their natural habitats, making Tanzania a preferred choice for wildlife enthusiasts.
blocks.html: Yes, Tanzania is well known as one of the best places to see the Big Five. You can watch these impressive animals (lion, leopard, elephant, rhinoceros and buffalo) in their natural surroundings, which is why so many wildlife lovers choose Tanzania.

blocks.orig: Absolutely, Tanzania is a safe and welcoming destination for travelers. The country offers a hospitable environment, especially in tourist areas like Arusha, and you can explore its beautiful landscapes and wildlife with confidence. Local people are friendly, and safety measures, such as keeping an eye on your belongings, are always advisable, just as you would in any other part of the world. Tanzania’s natural beauty and the warmth of its people make it a fantastic place to visit.
blocks.html: Yes, travellers will find Tanzania a safe and friendly destination. The atmosphere is welcoming, particularly in tourist areas such as Arusha, so you can enjoy its beautiful landscapes and wildlife with peace of mind. People are friendly, and it is always sensible to take ordinary precautions such as watching your belongings, just as you would anywhere else in the world. Thanks to Tanzania’s natural beauty and the warmth of its people, it is a wonderful country to visit.

blocks.orig: Tarangire National Park is well known for its big groups of elephants and the huge amount of giant baobab trees. These trees can live for hundreds of years and are actually a source of water for elephants in the dry season as they have a special technique to draw water from them. Besides, the Tarangire River is the only source of water in the dry season, which is why in this season in Tarangire you can see groups of up to 250 elephants next to many more animals!
blocks.html: Tarangire National Park is famous for its large herds of elephants and its great number of giant baobab trees. These trees can reach an age of several hundred years, and in the dry season elephants actually use them as a water source, drawing water out of them with a special technique. On top of that, the Tarangire River is the only water source during the dry season, which is why you can see herds of up to 250 elephants here at that time of year, alongside many other animals!

blocks.orig: Serengeti National Park is widely known as the place to go on safari, mainly because of the Great Migration that passes through here. The enormous, stampeding herds are impressive, as are the vast number of predators that live here: over four thousand lions, over 200 cheetahs, a thousand leopards, 3500 hyenas, and hundreds of wild dogs! And of course, plenty of other beautiful animals, which your guide will be delighted to search for together with you. Are you ready for this?
blocks.html: Serengeti National Park has a reputation as the place for a safari, largely thanks to the Great Migration that moves through the park. The huge, charging herds are a remarkable sight, and so is the large population of predators: more than four thousand lions, more than 200 cheetahs, a thousand leopards, 3500 hyenas and hundreds of wild dogs! Add to that many other beautiful animals, which your guide will gladly look for with you. Are you ready?

blocks.orig: Imagine crossing the grassy plains of northern Serengeti with your guide, and coming across millions of wildebeests and zebras, moaning and bleating as they attempt to cross a river full of crocodiles. This is the famous Mara River crossing of the Great Migration, a natural wonder that every year between July and October can be witnessed in the northern part of Serengeti National Park. This will be a nerve-racking event to watch - for did we mention the big cats waiting on the other side, just as hungry for meat as the herds are for greener pastures...?
blocks.html: Picture yourself driving across the grassy plains of the northern Serengeti with your guide and suddenly finding millions of wildebeests and zebras, groaning and bleating as they try to cross a river full of crocodiles. This is the well-known Mara River crossing of the Great Migration, a natural wonder you can see each year between July and October in the northern part of Serengeti National Park. Watching it is nerve-racking, because did we mention the big cats lying in wait on the far bank, every bit as hungry for meat as the herds are for fresher grazing...?

blocks.orig: The famous Ngorongoro Crater is one of Africa's seven natural wonders. The crater was formed two million years ago when a vast volcano erupted. The fertile lava has created a unique ecosystem, now home to the highest concentration of animals found anywhere in Africa! Once in the crater, thousands of animals such as lions, zebras, buffalos and black rhinos surround you, and the views are astounding – you won’t know where to look!
blocks.html: The renowned Ngorongoro Crater ranks among Africa's seven natural wonders. It came into being two million years ago, when a huge volcano erupted. The rich volcanic soil gave rise to a unique ecosystem that now supports the highest density of animals anywhere in Africa! Down in the crater you are surrounded by thousands of animals, including lions, zebras, buffalos and black rhinos, and the scenery is so spectacular that you won’t know where to look first!
